text: To entice is to draw someone or something in by making it appealing. You entice a cat with food, not by shouting at it. The headline says warming seas are enticing octopus to British waters, which is a loose way of putting it: the octopuses are not choosing to come, but the warmer water lets more of them survive there once currents carry their young in.

A burly person is big, heavy and strong-looking, in the way someone who lifts things all day often is. It is used almost only about men. The article opens with burly men in yellow overalls hauling crates, which tells you at once that this is hard physical work.

Overalls are tough one-piece work clothes worn over your ordinary clothes to keep them clean and dry. Fishermen wear waterproof ones, usually bright yellow so they can be seen easily. The yellow overalls in Brixham market are protection against water, fish guts and ice.

To lug something is to carry it when it is heavy and awkward, with effort. You lug a suitcase up the stairs; you do not lug a pencil. Saying the men lug around big white boxes tells you the crates of fish are heavy.

An offering usually means something given, but in business it means something put up for sale. A shop's offering is the range of goods it has. Here each crate contains a different offering, meaning a different kind of seafood on sale that morning.

Hake is a long, slim sea fish related to cod, common in the Atlantic and popular in Spain and Portugal. It is one of the ordinary catches sold at a British fish market. The article lists it alongside crab as an example of a normal, unremarkable thing in the crates.

If something is infamous, it is well known, but known for something bad. That is what separates it from famous: a famous singer is known for great songs, an infamous one for a scandal. The octopus is the infamous species here because Brixham's fishermen know it well and dislike it.

To balloon is to swell up fast and by a lot, the way a balloon does when you blow into it. People use it for numbers that shoot up: costs balloon, crowds balloon. Saying the number of octopuses has ballooned means it did not creep up, it multiplied quickly.

A tonne is a metric unit of weight equal to 1,000 kilograms, about the weight of a small car. It is spelled tonne to distinguish it from the slightly different American ton. Over 700 tonnes of octopus is therefore an enormous pile, roughly 700 small cars' worth.

In fishing, to land a catch means to bring it ashore and put it on the dock, where it gets weighed and recorded. It has nothing to do with landing a plane. Because every catch is written down as it is landed, we can say exactly how much octopus came into Brixham.

To sequester something is to set it apart and keep it away from everything else. Juries are sometimes sequestered in a hotel so nobody can talk to them. Here the octopus catch is sequestered in black boxes in its own room, kept separate from the rest of the market's fish.

Brixham is a fishing town on the south coast of Devon, in south-west England. It runs one of the busiest fish markets in the country, so what arrives there is a good indicator of what is living in the sea nearby. The whole article is built around what is showing up in Brixham's crates.

Calling something the bad boy of a field is a set English phrase for the troublemaker of the group, the one that breaks the rules and annoys everyone. It is half insult, half grudging respect. Octopuses are the bad boys of British fishing because they raid other fishermen's traps and make a mess.

Segregation means keeping one group apart from another. The word is most often used, very seriously, about the unjust separation of people by race in places such as the American South and South Africa. Here it is used in its plain, ordinary sense: the octopus crates are physically kept in a separate room.

To ravage something is to damage it severely and over a wide area. Fires ravage forests; diseases ravage populations. Saying octopuses have been ravaging the local shellfish population means they are eating enough crab and lobster to cut the numbers down sharply, not just nibbling at the edges.

To haul something is to pull or drag it, usually with effort and often upwards. Fishermen haul up pots from the seabed by rope or winch. The word also works as a noun for what you bring in, which is why a big catch is called a good haul.

A lobster pot is not a cooking pot. It is a cage-like trap, baited with fish, that is dropped to the seabed on a rope and hauled up later with lobster or crab inside. The problem in the article is that an octopus often gets into the pot first and eats whatever the trap caught.

A scallop is a shellfish that lives inside a pair of fan-shaped, ridged shells on the seabed. The muscle inside is expensive and prized by restaurants. King scallops are the large British kind, and they are one of the catches that has halved in the south-west.

A bloom is normally a flower, but scientists also use it for a sudden burst in the number of living things in water, as in an algal bloom that turns a pond green. The octopus bloom means a population explosion, not anything flowering. It is the scientific sense of the word, borrowed for a large animal.

Prominent means standing out so that you notice it before anything else. A prominent nose sticks out; a prominent scientist is one everybody has heard of. Calling the octopus bloom the most prominent example means it is the clearest and most obvious case of the change, not necessarily the largest.

To reside somewhere is to live there, in a settled, long-term way. It is a formal word, the one used on official forms rather than in conversation. Asking which creatures reside in British waters means asking which ones actually live there year-round, rather than passing through.

Here mean does not describe someone unkind and it is not the verb to mean. It is the maths word for the average: add up all the readings and divide by how many there are. The mean sea-surface temperature is what you get after averaging thousands of measurements taken around England.

Sea-surface temperature is the temperature of the top layer of the ocean, roughly the first few metres, which is the part the sun heats directly and where most sea creatures live. Satellites measure it from above and floating buoys measure it from in the water. Scientists always report it as a gap from a long-run average, which is why the article says 2.2C warmer than the previous 40 years rather than giving a plain temperature.

The English Channel is the stretch of sea between southern England and northern France, about 33 kilometres across at its narrowest. It is shallow and busy with ships. Young octopuses are far too small to swim it themselves, so the article says winds blew their young across it, meaning wind-driven currents carried them.

To thrive is to do more than merely survive: to grow well and multiply. A plant thrives in good soil; a business thrives when customers keep coming. Saying the young octopuses thrived in the newly warm waters means enough of them survived and grew to build up a big population.

The bluefin is the largest tuna, a powerful ocean fish that can weigh more than 400 kilograms and swim across whole oceans. It is extremely valuable, especially for sushi, which is exactly why it was caught so heavily. It has started reappearing off Britain after decades of near-absence.

Abundant means present in large amounts, more than enough. Rain is abundant in a rainforest; food is abundant at a feast. Saying bluefin tuna were once abundant off the British coast means they were not a rare treat but a common, everyday catch.

Overfishing means catching fish faster than the population can replace itself by breeding. Fewer adults are left, so fewer young are born the next year, so there are fewer adults again after that, and the decline speeds itself up. It is why bluefin tuna vanished from British waters even though the sea itself had not changed.

A landlubber is old sailors' slang for someone who stays on land and is useless at sea, and it is still used jokingly. Calling Britons land-lubbing is a joke setting them against the sea creatures in the rest of the sentence. The point is that people on land struggle in a heatwave too.

Aquatic means living or happening in water. An aquatic plant grows in a pond, and aquatic sports are the ones done in a pool. Long-term aquatic residents here just means the fish that have lived in these waters for a very long time.

To withstand something is to take it without breaking, giving way or being damaged. You withstand a force pressing on you: heat, cold, wind, weight. Cod and haddock cannot withstand the warmer water because above a certain temperature their bodies no longer work properly.

Marine biology is the study of life in the sea, so a marine biologist is a scientist who studies fish, shellfish and everything else that lives in the ocean. The Marine Biology Association is a long-established British research body based in Plymouth. Bryce Stewart is quoted because studying these shifts is his actual job.

In biology, an animal is adapted to conditions when its body works properly in them, because generations of its ancestors survived best there. A polar bear is adapted to cold. Saying cod are at the limits of what they are adapted to means the water is nearly too warm for their bodies to cope.

To retreat is to move back, away from something. An army retreats from a battle; a person retreats from an argument. When a species retreats north, no decision is involved: fewer survive and breed in the warm south, more do so further north, so over years the whole population sits further up the map.

Haddock is a white sea fish closely related to cod, and one of the two fish most often used in British fish and chips. It prefers cold water, which is the whole reason it appears in this article. As the sea off England has warmed, haddock have shifted northwards.

Handsomely here has nothing to do with good looks. When it describes money it means generously, by a large amount: you can be paid handsomely or profit handsomely. Saying some boats have profited handsomely from the octopus means they have made a great deal of money from it.

Infrastructure is the basic physical set-up that lets something work: roads, pipes, cables, ports, factories. It is the unglamorous background machinery, not the thing itself. Britain has the octopus but lacks the infrastructure for it, meaning there are not enough factories to clean and prepare the catch.

A plant is not always something green. In industry a plant is a factory or processing site, as in a power plant or a bottling plant. Saying Britain lacks enough plants to do so means it does not have enough factories to prepare octopus for sale, so the catch is shipped to Spain instead.

A staple is a basic food that people eat regularly and rely on, such as rice in much of Asia or bread in much of Europe. It is a different word from the small metal staple that holds paper. Saying battered octopus might become a seaside staple means it might turn into an ordinary, expected thing on the menu.

Battered here does not mean beaten up. Batter is a runny mixture of flour and liquid, and battered food has been dipped in it and fried, which is how the fish in British fish and chips is cooked. Battered octopus and chips would be octopus treated exactly like that fish.

In the long run is a standard English phrase meaning over a long stretch of time, once short-term ups and downs have evened out. It sets up a contrast with what is happening right now. The article uses it to say that although fishermen are struggling today, the industry as a whole will eventually be fine.

Plaice is a flatfish: it lies on the seabed with both eyes on its upper side, which is orange-spotted. It is a traditional British catch that prefers cooler water. It is listed with cod and haddock as one of the fish that may become scarcer around Britain.

A refugee is someone forced to leave home by danger such as war, and a climate refugee is someone forced out by drought, flooding or heat. The article applies the term to fish, which is a figure of speech rather than a fact: sardines and sea bass are not fleeing anywhere on purpose, they simply now survive and breed in seas that were once too cold for them.

Sweltering describes heat so heavy and humid that it is uncomfortable, the kind that makes you sweat sitting still. A sweltering afternoon is one nobody wants to play football in. Calling the seas the fish leave behind sweltering emphasises that the water is now genuinely too hot for them.

The Seychelles is a country of about 115 small islands in the Indian Ocean, north-east of Madagascar. It is tropical, and fishing and tourism are the main ways people earn a living there. It is the example of a hot country that has no warmer neighbour to receive new fish from.

Your livelihood is the work you earn your living from, the money that pays for your food and your home. It is stronger than the word job, because it points at what you depend on rather than a task you could drop tomorrow. Crab and lobster are the Brixham fishermen's livelihoods, so when those vanish from the pots their income vanishes too.
